---
title: "Solution: Topic Modelling with LDA"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(topicmodels)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 20000, seed = 602)
```

```{r prepare-words}
complaints <- health_data |>
  filter(!is.na(complaint_notes)) |>
  mutate(doc_id = row_number())

word_counts <- complaints |>
  unnest_tokens(word, complaint_notes) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  count(doc_id, word)

cat("Unique documents:", n_distinct(word_counts$doc_id), "\n")
cat("Unique terms:    ", n_distinct(word_counts$word), "\n")
```

## Task 1: Build the Document-Term Matrix

```{r task1-dtm}
dtm <- word_counts |>
  cast_dtm(doc_id, word, n)

dtm
# The DTM has one row per document, one column per term.
# Sparsity is high (>99%) because each complaint uses only ~10-20 unique
# words from a vocabulary of hundreds.
```

## Task 2: Fit a 5-topic LDA model

```{r task2-lda}
lda5 <- LDA(
  dtm,
  k       = 5,
  method  = "Gibbs",
  control = list(seed = 602, iter = 500, burnin = 100)
)
```

## Task 3: Extract and visualise word-topic probabilities (beta)

```{r task3-beta}
topics_beta <- tidy(lda5, matrix = "beta")

topics_beta |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(beta, n = 5) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r task3-plot}
topics_beta |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(beta, n = 10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(term = reorder_within(term, beta, topic)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = term, y = beta, fill = factor(topic))) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~topic, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Words per LDA Topic",
       x = "Term", y = "β (word-topic probability)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task3-label-topics}
# Topic labels based on top words (typical results with this simulator):
# Topic 1: "Billing Disputes"
#   Top words: charged, premium, statement, balance, notice, month, account
# Topic 2: "Slow Claim Processing"
#   Top words: claim, pending, submitted, processing, months, documents, incomplete
# Topic 3: "Coverage Gaps"
#   Top words: covered, dental, prescription, formulary, reimbursed, physiotherapy
# Topic 4: "Poor Customer Service"
#   Top words: service, hold, transferred, app, portal, emails, departments
# Topic 5: "Positive Feedback"
#   Top words: satisfied, professionally, promptly, renewed, clear, recommend, easy
# The labels match the 5 template categories used in the simulator, demonstrating
# that LDA can recover the latent structure without any supervision.
```

## Task 4: Document-topic probabilities and perplexity

```{r task4-gamma}
doc_topics <- tidy(lda5, matrix = "gamma")

doc_topics |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  summarise(mean_gamma = round(mean(gamma), 4)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_gamma))
# The topics should be approximately equally prevalent (~0.20 each) since the
# simulator samples from 5 templates with roughly equal probability.
```

```{r task4-perplexity}
perp_values <- sapply(3:7, function(k) {
  mod <- LDA(dtm, k = k, method = "Gibbs",
             control = list(seed = 602, iter = 200, burnin = 50))
  perplexity(mod)
})

tibble(K = 3:7, perplexity = perp_values) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = K, y = perplexity)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2, colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "LDA Perplexity vs. Number of Topics",
       x = "Number of Topics (K)", y = "Perplexity") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task4-best-k}
cat("Perplexity by K:\n")
tibble(K = 3:7, perplexity = round(perp_values, 1)) |> print()

# Perplexity typically shows an elbow around K = 5 for this dataset.
# K = 5 matches the 5 template categories in the simulator.
# Beyond K = 5, perplexity decreases more slowly and topics begin to split
# existing coherent themes into sub-themes, reducing interpretability.
# The perplexity elbow aligns with domain knowledge: 5 complaint categories.
```

## Task 5: Spark LDA on 500,000 complaint notes

```{r task5-spark-setup, eval=FALSE}
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local[*]", version = "3.4.1")

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_full <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
health_tbl  <- copy_to(sc, health_full,
                       name = "health_ins", overwrite = TRUE)

complaints_spark <- health_tbl |>
  filter(!is.na(complaint_notes)) |>
  mutate(doc_id = monotonically_increasing_id())

cat("Documents for LDA:", sdf_nrow(complaints_spark), "\n")
```

```{r task5-spark-pipeline, eval=FALSE}
tokenised  <- ft_tokenizer(complaints_spark,
                           input_col = "complaint_notes", output_col = "words_raw")
cleaned    <- ft_stop_words_remover(tokenised,
                                    input_col = "words_raw", output_col = "words")
cv_model   <- ft_count_vectorizer(cleaned,
                                  input_col = "words", output_col = "tf", min_df = 5)
tf_vectors <- ml_transform(cv_model, cleaned)

cat("Vocabulary size:", length(cv_model$vocabulary), "\n")
```

```{r task5-spark-lda, eval=FALSE}
lda_spark <- ml_lda(
  tf_vectors,
  features_col        = "tf",
  k                   = 5,
  max_iter            = 20,
  doc_concentration   = rep(1.0 / 5, 5),
  topic_concentration = 0.01
)

vocab     <- cv_model$vocabulary
topic_mat <- lda_spark$topics_matrix()

top_words_per_topic <- apply(topic_mat, 1, function(row) {
  vocab[order(row, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]]
})
cat("Top words per Spark LDA topic:\n")
print(top_words_per_topic)

# The 5 Spark LDA topics correspond to the same complaint categories but topic
# numbering is arbitrary — match topics by their top words, not their index.
# Spark LDA (Online LDA) uses variational EM rather than Gibbs sampling;
# max_iter = 20 mini-batch passes are sufficient for this templated corpus.
# For a real free-text corpus, 50-100 iterations and tuned hyperparameters
# would be needed to achieve comparable topic coherence.

spark_disconnect(sc)
```
